summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring continuous tube feeds was admitted to the surgery service for chronic gastrostomy-tube site pain after mechanical pulling of the tube. She underwent an open gastrostomy tube removal and replacement without intraoperative complications, recovered with initial PCA analgesia transitioned to hydromorphone via G-tube and scheduled acetaminophen, and remained hemodynamically stable and afebrile. She was initially NPO, then restarted on continuous tube feeds via the new G-tube on postoperative day 2 and was advanced to her home rate of 65 mL/hr, tolerating feeds and water by mouth. MRSA screening was negative, there were no bleeding concerns, and she was discharged home ambulatory with home nursing for daily dressing changes, instructions to avoid NSAIDs, crush medications for G-tube administration, adhere to lifting restrictions, and return precautions for infection or worsening symptoms.
